user.title: Meteo Tracker
user.description: Weather per person, based on each device tracker's live location, via the OpenWeather One Call API.

data_description.api_key: Create a free key at openweathermap.org and subscribe to 'One Call by Call' (1000 calls/day free with a spend limit). Which One Call version your key can reach is detected here: accounts created since OpenWeather stopped selling 3.0 get 4.0, older keys keep 3.0.
data_description.trackers: Each selected device tracker gets its own weather entity and sensor set, following that person's current location.
data_description.scan_interval_minutes: On One Call 3.0 a refresh costs 1 call per distinct location (5 min = ~288/day). On 4.0 the same picture is rebuilt from 6 requests, so the minimum is 10 minutes (~864/day). People standing together still share one set of calls.

reauth_confirm.title: Meteo Tracker: reconnect to OpenWeather
reauth_confirm.description:
OpenWeather is no longer accepting this key for One Call {version}.

Leave the field empty to re-check the key you already have — if your account can now only reach the other One Call version, this entry moves to it and keeps all of its entities and their history. Moving to 4.0 costs six requests per refresh instead of one, so the refresh interval is raised to 10 minutes if it is shorter.

Enter a key only if you want to replace the one in use.

data_description.api_key: Leave empty to keep the current key and only re-check which version it reaches.

error.invalid_auth: OpenWeather refused this key. Usually the key itself is fine but the 'One Call by Call' subscription is missing, or the key was created in the last couple of hours and is not active yet. The exact wording OpenWeather returned is in the Home Assistant log.
error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach OpenWeather. Check your internet connection.
error.rate_limited: OpenWeather rejected the request: call limit reached.
error.no_trackers: Select at least one device tracker.
error.interval_too_low_v4: One Call 4.0 needs six requests per refresh, so anything under 10 minutes runs past the 1000 calls/day free tier. OpenWeather only updates 4.0 every 10 minutes, so a shorter interval would buy duplicate data.
error.interval_too_low: Refresh interval is shorter than this API version allows.
error.version_unavailable: OpenWeather refused your key for that One Call version. You need a separate subscription for each version — subscribing to one does not extend to the other. A subscription activated in the last couple of hours may also not be live yet. The exact wording OpenWeather returned is in the Home Assistant log.

abort.reauth_successful: Reconnected. The entry kept its entities and history.

init.description:
This entry uses **One Call {version}**. Requests per refresh, per distinct location: **{per_refresh}**. Distinct locations right now: **{locations}**.

Daily One Call requests by interval — ✅ within the free {free}/day, ⚠️ past it:

{budget}

That allowance belongs to your **OpenWeather account**, not to this installation: every key on the account and every Home Assistant using them draw from the same {free}. Weather alerts cost one extra request each on 4.0. Air quality uses a separate free API and is not counted here.
